\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-20},
  title = {Personal data stays on a public DagsHub remote},
  note = {\textbf{Absorbs EDN-34 and EDN-37} (2026-09-30): the raw Parquet keeps its personal-data columns, and the seller key is an unsalted hash.},
  date = {2026-09-29},
  milestone = {M2: Reproducibility},
  topic = {Data Versioning, Privacy},
  participants = {@lukas2510; confirmation by the full team is pending until the laboratory session of 2026-10-13},
  decision = {The DagsHub repository that serves as DVC remote and MLflow server stays public.
The raw Parquet of the \texttt{download} stage keeps the seven personal-data columns of the published file and is pushed like any stage output; preprocessing removes them.
\texttt{seller\_\allowbreak{}group\_\allowbreak{}id} is an unsalted hash that groups the split and anonymises nothing, as the dataset card says.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item A private repository: every grader and supervisor needs a collaborator entry, and the identical file stays public on Zenodo.
\item \texttt{push: false} on the raw Parquet: each machine regenerates the pipeline's first artefact, which puts byte-identical reproduction at risk.
\item A secret pepper in the hash: the split would depend on a secret outside the repository, so a clean clone could not reproduce it.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} The same data is public under the pinned Zenodo DOI, so the added exposure is small.
It is not nothing: hosting a copy makes the team a publisher of that personal data in its own right.
We accept this risk and revisit it once we host data that is not public elsewhere.},
  ai = {Information seeking, Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation},
  response = {Used as input for further analysis},
  assessment = {AI showed that the premise ``the repository is private'' was false and laid out both options without recommending one; Lukas decided.
For the Parquet, AI preferred removing the columns in \texttt{download}; Lukas took the simpler option.
An adversarial AI review inverted every seller id with a dictionary, so we corrected the claim instead of adding a pepper.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code sessions of 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30 (reviews of PR \#48 and PR \#56); Lukas answered (translated from German): ``we keep it public''.},
  evidence = {\href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/docs/docs/dataset-card.md}{Dataset card}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/pull/26}{PR \#26}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/pull/48}{PR \#48}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/pull/56}{PR \#56}.},
